correctness.rationale: For H_{bar psi} with psi(z)=az+bz² and a,b complex, the Hankel matrix on span{1,z} is [[bar a,bar b],[bar b,0]], giving ||H||=(|a|+sqrt(|a|²+4|b|²))/2. Direct Szego-kernel action gives K(H)²=max_{0<=r<=1}(1-r²)((|a|+|b|r)²+|b|²) with angular alignment. For both coefficients nonzero set t=|a|/|b| and x=(t+sqrt(t²+4))/2; radial derivative t-t²r-3tr²-2r³ is strictly decreasing and has exactly one interior zero. Differentiating the optimized squared ratio yields two branches s=t+r=x or 1/x. Substituting into the radial equation excludes s=x and forces x²=3/2, t=r=1/sqrt6 on s=1/x. Since ratio tends to 1 as t->0 and t->infty, the unique stationary point is global minimum squared 25/27, i.e. 5/(3sqrt3); monomial cases have ratio 1. Equality phases follow triangle equality. Independent symbolic check verified both branch factorizations; numerical one-dimensional search and 301-point logarithmic grid corroborated norm ratio about 0.96225044865, not a continuum proof.
